findings.checklist_item: Reconcile the project-LLM glob save-validation with ADR 0074: treat `applies_to: []`/absent as the legal 'ungated' spelling for project code-review criteria rather than rejecting it, and scope any non-empty-glob requirement so it does not contradict overlay.py/_validate_applies_to.
evidence: docs/adr/0074-code-review-overlay-escalation.md:97 — 'project criterion (project.<name>): applies_to: [] means ungated — runs on every review'
src/rebar/llm/criteria/overlay.py:197-198 — 'An empty LIST stays legal: that is the deliberate "ungated" spelling this repo's own overlay uses.'
src/rebar/llm/code_review/registry.py:333 — project_criterion_applies: 'An EMPTY (or absent) glob list means UNGATED — the criterion runs on every review.'
tests/unit/test_project_review_phase_boundaries.py:233-236 — the repo's own criterion asserts `applies_to == []`
findings.finding: The save-validation rule rejects `applies_to: []`/missing for project code-review LLM criteria, but that empty list is a documented, load-bearing legal spelling meaning UNGATED for project criteria (ADR 0074; overlay.py `_validate_applies_to` deliberately keeps it legal; this repo's own `project.review-phase-boundaries` uses it). The rule would make the editor reject a value the overlay compiler accepts and depends on, creating the second conflicting policy authority the plan set out to prevent.
findings.location: Approach section ("a new `project.*` code-review LLM criterion must have a non-empty list of non-empty repository-relative `applies_to` globs") and AC line 3
scenarios: Author edits/re-saves the existing `project.review-phase-boundaries` criterion via the editor and is blocked, or is forced to change its runtime gating semantics
A project author who wants an always-on project criterion is refused the value the overlay loader treats as canonical
findings.suggested_fix: Accept an explicit empty list (ungated) as valid for project code-review criteria; only reject malformed shapes (non-list, non-string/blank elements) — mirroring `_validate_applies_to` — so the editor and overlay loader share one rule.

findings.checklist_item: State whether repository-wide intent must map to `[]` (ungated) or `["**"]` (glob-gated) and note they differ on empty-diff reviews, so the editor's remedy does not silently change dispatch semantics.
evidence: tests/unit/test_code_review_project_criteria.py:856 — `([], ["anything.txt"], True)`
tests/unit/test_code_review_project_criteria.py:859 — `(["**/*.py"], [], False)` (a glob does not fire on an empty diff)
src/rebar/llm/code_review/registry.py:341-343 — `if not globs: return True` (empty = always applies; else must match a changed file)
findings.finding: The prescribed `["**"]` remedy is not behaviorally equivalent to the `[]` (ungated) value it is meant to replace: a `["**"]` glob requires at least one matching changed file, whereas `[]` dispatches unconditionally (including empty-diff reviews). Steering authors to `["**"]` silently changes runtime dispatch semantics and cannot express the always-on intent.
findings.location: Approach section ("rejects an empty/missing selector with the exact `["**"]` repository-wide remedy") and AC line 3
scenarios: A review with no changed files: a `[]` criterion runs; the `["**"]`-migrated criterion does not
